# Obtain Queue

![Obtain Queue function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/synchronization/queue/01_Obtain%20Queue.svg)

[Synchronization functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Creates an anonymous FIFO when name is empty, or obtains an additional access to a same-application named FIFO with exactly the complete element type. The type specimen is not an inserted message. Capacity defaults to -1; an existing named capacity is preserved. Queue&lt;T&gt; is an execution resource reference; element is the ordinary T value. Public FROG target compilation remains unavailable.

## Studio authoring profile

Contract status: **partial**. The connector below describes Studio authoring; execution availability is stated separately.

Creates an anonymous FIFO when name is empty, or obtains an additional access to a same-application named FIFO with exactly the complete element type. The type specimen is not an inserted message. Capacity defaults to -1; an existing named capacity is preserved.

## Queue behavior

The optional element data type is a type specimen, not a first message. With no specimen, Studio resolves T to F64. An empty name creates a new anonymous FIFO. A nonempty name obtains an independent access to the same application queue only when the entire element schema matches; an existing queue keeps its capacity. Capacity -1 is unbounded.

Queue&lt;T&gt; is a nominal execution-resource access reference. The complete T schema is invariant; an Array, Cluster or Enum message remains one T value. Collection outputs add one outer rank-1 Array.

## Types and connection rules

Queue&lt;T&gt; is a nominal execution-resource reference distinct from object/File references. The complete T is invariant; only the collection output adds an outer rank-1 Array.

- Type resolution: `custom_resolver`; result expression: `resolve:frog.studio.synchronization.queue.type-resolution@1`.
- Implicit coercion: not enabled by this resolver; individual port policies remain explicit.
- Arrays: accepted; lifting policy: `none`.

One queued element may itself be an Array, Cluster or Enum; preserve its complete schema and message boundary. No element-wise lifting or array flattening.

**Input count:** 5; this contract does not enable variadic inputs.

Port order: `element_type` → `name` → `max_size` → `create_if_not_found` → `error_in`.
